questions.q: If a toy train travels 5 cm every 1 second, how far will it travel in 4 seconds if it is in uniform motion?
questions.a: It will travel 20 cm. If a student answers differently, it reveals they do not understand that "equal distances in equal intervals of time" means the distance must be multiplied by the time elapsed.

questions.q: A car’s distance-time graph is a perfectly straight, sloped line. What does this tell you about the car's speed?
questions.a: The speed is constant. If a student says the speed is increasing, they are confusing a straight line with a curved line, failing to grasp that a constant slope means a constant rate of change.

questions.q: A bus travels 100 km in 2 hours. Calculate its speed.
questions.a: Speed = Distance / Time = 100 km / 2 h = 50 km/h. If a student multiplies instead of divides, they are misapplying the basic algebraic relationship between the three variables.

questions.q: Two cars, A and B, are moving in uniform motion. Car A has a steeper line on the graph than Car B. Which car is faster?
questions.a: Car A is faster. If a student guesses Car B, they do not understand that the "steepness" (slope) of the line represents how much distance is covered per unit of time.

questions.q: If a cyclist covers 10m in the first second, 10m in the second, and 15m in the third, is this uniform motion? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it is not uniform motion because the distance covered is not equal for every equal time interval. A wrong answer shows the student has not grasped the "equal distance" requirement of the definition.

questions.q: Design a simple experiment to prove a rolling marble is in uniform motion. What would you look for in your data?
questions.a: Measure the marble's position at every 1-second interval. To show uniform motion, the difference in distance between each interval must be identical. A poor answer fails to mention the necessity of consistent time intervals.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Uniform motion occurs when an object moves in a straight line at a constant speed, covering equal ______ in equal intervals of time.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are riding a bicycle on a long, ______, empty road, and you keep your legs moving at the exact same pace the entire time.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to calculate speed given distance and time, and identify uniform motion by observing if distance increases by the same amount for every equal unit of time.
